subject.title: tools.deny not enforced for claude-cli backend MCP — agents can call denied MCP tools

question: What enforcement contract should OpenClaw use for `tools.deny` and narrower MCP tool policy when a CLI backend like `claude-cli` can only receive generated server config or downstream CLI allow/deny flags?
rationale: The bug is source-proven, but the previous fix attempt showed that representing OpenClaw's exact/wildcard tool policy at a CLI MCP handoff can either fix denial or accidentally widen allowed access unless maintainers choose the permanent security boundary.

options.title: Filter before CLI handoff
options.body: Resolve the per-agent effective MCP policy before generating CLI MCP config, preserve exact-tool restrictions without server-wide widening, and fail closed when the backend cannot represent the restriction.

options.title: Map to Claude flags
options.body: Use Claude-specific `--disallowedTools` mappings for deny entries while keeping the generated server config broad, accepting a provider-specific enforcement path that needs upstream contract proof.

options.title: Warn instead of enforce
options.body: Document and doctor-warn that CLI MCP tool policy is not enforced, leaving current runtime behavior intact but no longer treating `tools.deny` as a hard boundary for this backend.

recommendation.title: Filter before CLI handoff
recommendation.body: Resolve the per-agent effective MCP policy before generating CLI MCP config, preserve exact-tool restrictions without server-wide widening, and fail closed when the backend cannot represent the restriction.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal points to steipete's prior work on the Claude CLI loopback MCP bridge and shared bundle MCP config surface where the security boundary must be settled.
